shortDescription: Oil refiners Valero Energy NYSE:VLO and Marathon Petroleum NYSE:MPC trade modestly lower Tuesday as Jefferies downgraded shares of both companies to Hold from Buy with respective $401 and $413 price targets, saying valuations look stretched after the two companies have more than doubled during the…

children: trade modestly lower Tuesday as Jefferies downgraded shares of both companies to Hold from Buy with respective $401 and $413 price targets, saying valuations look stretched after the two companies have more than doubled during the past year.

"With no clear solution to tight [refining] fundamentals... what could derail the current cycle? We believe product prices will need to rise higher and stay elevated to spur demand destruction, or government intervention may be necessary," according to Jefferies analysts led by Lloyd Byrne.

"Investor focus is on a U.S. product export ban into midterms with political support increasing," the analyst wrote. "While this would be detrimental to global stability and would have economic ramifications for the U.S., with global powers increasingly prioritizing national interests, there is potential for the U.S. to follow suit."

Byrne said he believes the risk-reward for refiners supports holding existing positions while waiting for volatility to add to positions, and even with elevated strip pricing through 2029, current share prices imply 2030 midcycle margins near 2025 levels.

title: Valero, Marathon cut at Jefferies, supporting less refining exposure after big gains
